parts.name: Interpubic disc
parts.attachment_or_location: between the two pubic symphyseal (articular) surfaces
parts.function_note: unlike a synovial joint, the pubic symphysis is a secondary cartilaginous joint (symphysis): each pubic bone's articular surface is itself covered in hyaline cartilage, and this fibrocartilaginous disc between them can contain a small, non-synovial-lined cavity/cleft -- documented in roughly one in ten adult specimens by systematic review, concentrated in the disc's posterosuperior portion, so a minority rather than majority finding -- a structural resemblance to, but not a true, synovial joint.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Becker I, Woodley SJ, Stringer MD (2010) 'The adult human pubic symphysis: a systematic review.' J Anat 217(5):475-487 -- systematic review finding the interpubic disc cleft in a minority (roughly one in ten) of adult specimens, concentrated in the posterosuperior portion of the disc, not the majority implied by 'often' (frequency corrected after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).

function: Permits slight symphyseal motion (increased physiologically during pregnancy/parturition under hormonal relaxation), reinforced by the superior and arcuate pubic ligaments.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
